title: Departure synthesis workbook & re-engage playbook
content:
Purpose:
This is a working workbook for synthesizing client departures, surface root causes, and lay out a practical re-engagement sequence. Designed to be used by CSM + Solutions during the 10 business days after a confirmed loss and then adapted into the QBR/Executive recap if re-engagement is pursued.

Quick summary fields (fill top-of-doc):
- Account name: 
- ARR at churn: 
- Contract end / churn date: 
- CSM / AE / Solutions owner(s): 
- Primary stated reason for leaving (customer quote): 
- Net retention outcome (e.g., re-signed, downgraded, churn): 
- Decision maker(s) identified: 

1) Fast facts (one-liner + single-line evidence)
- Most likely proximate cause: [product / price / performance / org-change / compliance / procurement / competitor] — evidence: ticket count, latency SLO violations, contract notes.
- Most likely root systemic cause: [onboarding gaps / feature mismatch / escalation handling / lack of ROI metric / procurement timing] — evidence pointer: <link>.
- Customer sentiment at exit: 

2) Engagement timeline (concise, bullet time sequence)
- T-180: initial POC kickoff (owner: AE)
- T-120: first deployment; telemetry shows 40% lower success-rate on batch jobs (link to telemetry)
- T-90: scope change request (PRJ-123) — Solutions scoped extra work (estimate +$40k)
- T-45: support ticket cascade (SUP-298, SUP-301) unresolved beyond SLA
- T-14: procurement delay and legal redline on data residency
- T-3: verbal notice from sponsor (reason: price/ops risk)
- D0: official non-renewal sent by procurement

3) Data & signal inventory (where we looked to validate causes)
- Usage: token/embedding volumes, month-over-month delta, peak concurrency windows (links to dashboard).
- Performance: p95 latency spikes by date (attach trace ids).
- Support: ticket backlog and severity map (SUP-* list).
- Exec engagement: number & timing of sponsor-level meetings.
- Commercial: quotes/discount history, renewal timeline, procurement emails.
- Competitor activity: demo dates, public commitments.

4) Root cause hypotheses (ranked) — for each, write supporting evidence and counter-evidence
- Hypothesis A: Persistent perf regressions during peak windows caused operations risk perception.
  - Evidence: p95 latency spiked > SLA 3x in last 90 days; 2 major incidents; customer incident playbook not aligned.
  - Counter-evidence: errors were transient and correlated with customer-side config change; not observed in other tenants.
- Hypothesis B: Misaligned expectations during onboarding -> feature gaps for core workflow.
  - Evidence: documented scope-creep in onboarding notes; two features in roadmap not delivered before renewal.
  - Counter-evidence: customer accepted roadmap timelines in checklist sign-off.
- Hypothesis C: Price pressure + procurement re-org led to reprioritization.
  - Evidence: procurement asked for multi-vendor RFx; aggressive competitor discounting logged.
  - Counter-evidence: total cost of ownership analysis still favored Redwood in 12-month horizon.

5) Counterfactual scenarios (brief, pragmatic):
- CF1: If we had implemented a targeted perf mitigation (KV cache tweak + bumped batch size) 45 days earlier, incident frequency would likely reduce by ~60% and give time for PO to re-evaluate risk.
- CF2: If Solutions had shipped the two small onboarding features in-sprint and provided a short-term workaround, product fit signal would be stronger in QBRs and usage would have increased.
- CF3: If commercial had created a short-term bridge discount tied to specific SLAs, procurement might have extended evaluation by 3 months.
- For each CF, list required owners, time-to-delivery, and cost estimate.

6) Re-engage playbook (prioritized actions for 90/60/30 day windows)
- 90-day plan (restore trust):
  - Immediate: schedule a 30-min technical teardown with SRE + Solutions to walk through incident traces (owner: SRE lead, target: 7 days).
  - Product: deliver engineering triage plan with commit dates for the 2 onboarding items (owner: PM).
  - Commercial: send a no-strings 60-day trial extension with scoped SLA credits tied to measurable perf KPIs (owner: AE).
- 60-day plan (rebuild value):
  - Joint ROI workshop with customer ops and finance to quantify runway benefits.
  - Deploy a performance dashboard just for the customer (shared view) and weekly sync.
- 30-day plan (convert):
  - Executive check-in with sponsor + short proposal with phased pricing that aligns to achieved SLAs.

7) Renewal tracker (simple tabular template to copy into sheet)
Columns (comma-separated): Account, ARR, Contract End, Current Status, Primary Reason, Last Engagement Date, Next Action, Owner, Re-engage Deadline, Notes
Example row: AcmeCo, $120k, 2026-02-28, non-renewed, perf-risk, 2026-01-06, schedule-tech-teardown, Aisha P, 2026-03-10, PRJ-123 impact analysis pending

8) QBR summary bullets (what to include in a retrospective QBR slide)
- Objective summary (1 line): why we lost the renewal.
- Evidence stack (metrics + qualitative): usage delta, incident count, procurement timeline.
- Counterfactuals considered (2–3).
- Concrete commitments to prevent recurrence (team-level changes).
- Proposed re-engage ask and success metrics.

9) Communications and escalation map
- Low-friction comms: weekly status in #cs-account-health, copy of perf dashboard.
- Sponsor escalation: schedule a 1:1 exec sync (owner: Head of CS).
- Internal escalation: if SLA metrics exceed thresholds after re-engage, trigger SRT (Service Recovery Team) runbook.

10) Action log (to be maintained until closed)
- [ ] 7d: SRE technical teardown scheduled (owner: Jon R, due: 2026-02-22)
- [ ] 14d: PM roadmap commit and interim workaround published (owner: Priya S, due: 2026-03-01)
- [ ] 21d: Commercial bridge offer sent (owner: Marco A, due: 2026-03-05)

11) Evidence attachments & where to find them (links and quick notes)
- Telemetry dashboard: <link> (contains p95 by day)
- Support ticket digest: SUP-298, SUP-301 (link to ticket exports)
- Contract / procurement emails: drive:/shared_drives/customer-success/contracts/AcmeCo-renewal-2026

Notes to reviewer / TODOs:
- Confirm whether legal approved trial-extension template (legal@redwood).
- Ask Product Ops for a short blameless incident postmortem (we only have a high-level incident log).
- Determine if competitor discounting evidence can be redacted for executive summary.

How to use this workbook:
- Step 1: Populate the top quick facts and timeline within 48 hours of confirmed non-renewal.
- Step 2: Assign evidence owners and gather telemetry within 5 business days.
- Step 3: Draft counterfactuals and pick 1–2 fast experiments to propose in re-engage flow.
- Step 4: Move the Renewal tracker row into the shared Renewal sheet and escalate per the map above.

Version notes: draft v0.9 — intended to standardize post-exit analysis and give CSMs an action-first re-engage checklist.
